questions.stem: A linear model has 1,800 variables and 900 constraints. Using the free tiers as published on the pages this lesson opened, which of Gurobi's pip license, CPLEX Community Edition and the Xpress Community License accept it?

options.text: All three, since each free tier allows a few thousand variables
options.says: CPLEX Community Edition stops at 1,000 variables, and this model has 1,800.

options.text: Gurobi's and Xpress's, since CPLEX's tier stops at 1,000 variables
options.says: Right: 1,800 and 900 are within Gurobi's 2,000 each, and 2,700 is within Xpress's 5,000 rows plus columns.

options.text: Only Xpress's, since Gurobi's tier caps variables plus constraints at 2,000
options.says: Gurobi's caps are 2,000 variables and 2,000 linear constraints separately; it is Xpress that caps the sum.

options.text: None of them, since every free tier stops below 1,000 variables
options.says: Only CPLEX stops at 1,000; GridCap medium's timing model, 887 by 469, fits all three.

origin.section: Free Commercial Tiers Stop at a Size GridCap Outgrows

questions.stem: A nightly solver job runs on AWS Batch on Fargate inside a private network with no route out to the internet. The team gives it a Gurobi Web License Service (WLS) license. What happens when the job starts?

options.text: It solves, since a container that starts fresh each night needs no license
options.says: A container does not remove licensing; it is a fresh machine, which a machine-bound license cannot accept.

options.text: It solves, since the WLS token is fetched once when the image is built
options.says: The container fetches and renews its token at start, and a license is never baked into an image.

options.text: It cannot get a license, since WLS must reach Gurobi's servers to work
options.says: Right: WLS needs the internet; inside this network only a token server inside it would work.

options.text: It cannot get a license, since WLS works only with an Academic license
options.says: The container pages say the opposite: Academic and NODE licenses are the ones that do not work in containers.

origin.section: In a Container, a Commercial License Needs a Route Out

questions.stem: A commercial product has shipped with SCIP 8.0.2 pinned for years. A new legal review asks whether that pin raises a license question. What does this lesson say?

options.text: Yes, since every release to 8.0.2 had the ZIB Academic License
options.says: Right: SCIP moved to Apache 2.0 with 8.0.3; earlier releases keep the academic license.

options.text: Yes, since every SCIP release needs a license server to solve
options.says: SCIP solved in the offline runner with no network and no license server.

options.text: No, since every SCIP release has been under the Apache 2.0 license
options.says: Only releases from 8.0.3 are Apache 2.0, by the SCIP site.

options.text: No, since every open-source license allows any use without terms
options.says: Permissive licenses still have terms about notices and redistribution, and SCIP's academic license had more.

origin.section: Open-Source Solvers Cost Nothing to License, and Their Licenses Still Have Terms
